turns.content: A benzene ring bears a carboxylic acid together with formyl, cyano, methoxy, hydroxy, and dimethylamino substituents. Which parent structure is used for IUPAC naming, and which carbon is position 1?

Work out the possible locants with the carboxylic-acid carbon as position 1: carboxylic acid, formyl, and cyano are mutually meta; methoxy is para to the acid; hydroxy and dimethylamino are ortho to it; and methoxy and hydroxy are each ortho to cyano. Keep both numbering directions as candidates for comparison with the remaining constraints.
Use the final ortho constraints to select the numbering direction and assign locants to all five prefixes.
Apply the IUPAC prefix-ordering rule to hydroxy, formyl, methoxy, cyano, and dimethylamino in the written name.
Combine the parent, locants, and prefix order into a complete systematic name.
Check that the parent, locants, prefix ordering, and punctuation are internally consistent.
Write the resulting complete systematic name.
